# `sqlite-utils [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...`

Commands for interacting with a SQLite database

Options:
- `--version`: Show the version and exit.

Default command: `query`. When the first argument is not a command name, `sqlite-utils ARGS...` runs `sqlite-utils query ARGS...`.

Commands:
- `sqlite-utils add-column`: Add a column to the specified table
- `sqlite-utils add-foreign-key`: Add a new foreign key constraint to an existing table
- `sqlite-utils add-foreign-keys`: Add multiple new foreign key constraints to a database
- `sqlite-utils add-geometry-column`: Add a SpatiaLite geometry column to an existing table.
- `sqlite-utils analyze`: Run ANALYZE against the whole database, or against specific named indexes and tables
- `sqlite-utils analyze-tables`: Analyze the columns in one or more tables
- `sqlite-utils bulk`: Execute parameterized SQL against the provided list of documents.
- `sqlite-utils convert`: Convert columns using Python code you supply.
- `sqlite-utils create-database`: Create a new empty database file
- `sqlite-utils create-index`: Add an index to the specified table for the specified columns
- `sqlite-utils create-spatial-index`: Create a spatial index on a SpatiaLite geometry column.
- `sqlite-utils create-table`: Add a table with the specified columns.
- `sqlite-utils create-view`: Create a view for the provided SELECT query
- `sqlite-utils disable-fts`: Disable full-text search for specific table
- `sqlite-utils disable-wal`: Disable WAL for database files
- `sqlite-utils drop-index`: Drop an index by index name from the specified table
- `sqlite-utils drop-table`: Drop the specified table
- `sqlite-utils drop-view`: Drop the specified view
- `sqlite-utils dump`: Output a SQL dump of the schema and full contents of the database
- `sqlite-utils duplicate`: Create a duplicate of this table, copying across the schema and all row data.
- `sqlite-utils enable-counts`: Configure triggers to update a _counts table with row counts
- `sqlite-utils enable-fts`: Enable full-text search for specific table and columns
- `sqlite-utils enable-wal`: Enable WAL for database files
- `sqlite-utils extract`: Extract one or more columns into a separate table
- `sqlite-utils index-foreign-keys`: Ensure every foreign key column has an index on it
- `sqlite-utils indexes`: Show indexes for the whole database or specific tables
- `sqlite-utils insert`: Insert records from FILE into a table, creating the table if it does not already exist.
- `sqlite-utils insert-files`: Insert one or more files using BLOB columns in the specified table
- `sqlite-utils install`: Install packages from PyPI into the same environment as sqlite-utils
- `sqlite-utils memory`: Execute SQL query against an in-memory database, optionally populated by imported data
- `sqlite-utils migrate`: Apply pending database migrations.
- `sqlite-utils optimize`: Optimize all full-text search tables and then run VACUUM - should shrink the database file
- `sqlite-utils plugins`: List installed plugins
- `sqlite-utils populate-fts`: Re-populate full-text search for specific table and columns
- `sqlite-utils query` (default command): Execute SQL query and return the results as JSON
- `sqlite-utils rebuild-fts`: Rebuild all or specific full-text search tables
- `sqlite-utils rename-table`: Rename this table.
- `sqlite-utils reset-counts`: Reset calculated counts in the _counts table
- `sqlite-utils rows`: Output all rows in the specified table
- `sqlite-utils schema`: Show full schema for this database or for specified tables
- `sqlite-utils search`: Execute a full-text search against this table
- `sqlite-utils tables`: List the tables in the database
- `sqlite-utils transform`: Transform a table beyond the capabilities of ALTER TABLE
- `sqlite-utils triggers`: Show triggers configured in this database
- `sqlite-utils uninstall`: Uninstall Python packages from the sqlite-utils environment
- `sqlite-utils upsert`: Upsert records based on their primary key.
- `sqlite-utils vacuum`: Run VACUUM against the database
- `sqlite-utils views`: List the views in the database

Shared options (listed by name in the commands that accept them):
- `--load-extension TEXT` (repeatable): Path to SQLite extension, with optional :entrypoint
- `--functions TEXT` (repeatable): Python code or a file path defining custom SQL functions; can be used multiple times
- `--flatten`: Flatten nested JSON objects, so {"a": {"b": 1}} becomes {"a_b": 1}
- `--lines`: Treat each line as a single value called 'line'
- `--encoding TEXT`: Character encoding for input, defaults to utf-8
- `--not-null TEXT` (repeatable): Columns that should be created as NOT NULL
- `--default TEXT TEXT` (repeatable): Default value that should be set for a column
- `--no-headers`: Omit headers from CSV/TSV and table/--fmt output
- `--fmt TEXT`: Table format - one of asciidoc, colon_grid, double_grid, double_outline, fancy_grid, fancy_outline, github, grid, heavy_grid, heavy_outline, html, jira, latex, latex_booktabs, latex_longtable, latex_raw, mediawiki, mixed_grid, mixed_outline, moinmoin, orgtbl, outline, pipe, plain, presto, pretty, psql, rounded_grid, rounded_outline, rst, simple, simple_grid, simple_outline, textile, tsv, unsafehtml, youtrack
- `--json-cols`: Detect JSON cols and output them as JSON, not escaped strings
- `--ascii`: Escape non-ASCII characters in JSON output as \uXXXX

## `sqlite-utils add-column [OPTIONS] PATH TABLE COL_NAME [COL_TYPE]`

Add a column to the specified table

Example:

    sqlite-utils add-column chickens.db chickens weight float

Arguments:
- `PATH` (file; required)
- `TABLE` (text; required)
- `COL_NAME` (text; required)
- `[COL_TYPE]` (one of: integer, int, float, real, text, str, blob, bytes, any; case-insensitive)

Options:
- `--fk TEXT`: Table to reference as a foreign key
- `--fk-col TEXT`: Referenced column on that foreign key table - if omitted will automatically use the primary key
- `--not-null-default TEXT`: Add NOT NULL DEFAULT 'TEXT' constraint
- `--ignore`: If column already exists, do nothing
- Shared options: `--load-extension`

## `sqlite-utils add-geometry-column [OPTIONS] DB_PATH TABLE COLUMN_NAME`

Add a SpatiaLite geometry column to an existing table. Requires SpatiaLite extension.



By default, this command will try to load the SpatiaLite extension from usual paths.
To load it from a specific path, use --load-extension.

Arguments:
- `DB_PATH` (file; required)
- `TABLE` (text; required)
- `COLUMN_NAME` (text; required)

Options:
- `-t, --type [point|linestring|polygon|multipoint|multilinestring|multipolygon|geometrycollection|geometry]` (case-insensitive; default: GEOMETRY): Specify a geometry type for this column.
- `--srid INT` (default: 4326): Spatial Reference ID. See https://spatialreference.org for details on specific projections.
- `--dimensions TEXT` (default: XY): Coordinate dimensions. Use XYZ for three-dimensional geometries.
- `--not-null`: Add a NOT NULL constraint.
- Shared options: `--load-extension`

## `sqlite-utils bulk [OPTIONS] PATH SQL FILE`

Execute parameterized SQL against the provided list of documents.

Example:

    echo '[
        {"id": 1, "name": "Lila2"},
        {"id": 2, "name": "Suna2"}
    ]' | sqlite-utils bulk data.db '
        update chickens set name = :name where id = :id
    ' -

Arguments:
- `PATH` (file; required)
- `SQL` (text; required)
- `FILE` (file; required)

Options:
- `--batch-size INT` (default: 100): Commit every X records
- `--nl`: Expect newline-delimited JSON
- `-c, --csv`: Expect CSV input
- `--tsv`: Expect TSV input
- `--empty-null`: Treat empty strings as NULL
- `--text`: Treat input as a single value called 'text'
- `--convert TEXT`: Python code to convert each item
- `--import TEXT` (repeatable): Python modules to import
- `--delimiter TEXT`: Delimiter to use for CSV files
- `--quotechar TEXT`: Quote character to use for CSV/TSV
- `--sniff`: Detect delimiter and quote character
- `--no-headers`: CSV file has no header row
- Shared options: `--functions`, `--flatten`, `--lines`, `--encoding`, `--load-extension`

## `sqlite-utils convert [OPTIONS] DB_PATH TABLE COLUMNS... CODE`

Convert columns using Python code you supply. For example:

sqlite-utils convert my.db mytable mycolumn \
    '"\n".join(textwrap.wrap(value, 10))' \
    --import=textwrap

"value" is a variable with the column value to be converted.

CODE can also be a reference to a callable that takes the value, for example:

sqlite-utils convert my.db mytable date r.parsedate
sqlite-utils convert my.db mytable data json.loads --import json

Use "-" for CODE to read Python code from standard input.

The following common operations are available as recipe functions:

r.jsonsplit(value: 'str', delimiter: 'str' = ',', type: 'Callable[[str], object]' = <class 'str'>) -> 'str'

Convert a string like a,b,c into a JSON array ["a", "b", "c"]

r.parsedate(value: 'str', dayfirst: 'bool' = False, yearfirst: 'bool' = False, errors: 'object | None' = None) -> 'str | None'

Parse a date and convert it to ISO date format: yyyy-mm-dd
- dayfirst=True: treat xx as the day in xx/yy/zz
- yearfirst=True: treat xx as the year in xx/yy/zz
- errors=r.IGNORE to ignore values that cannot be parsed
- errors=r.SET_NULL to set values that cannot be parsed to null

r.parsedatetime(value: 'str', dayfirst: 'bool' = False, yearfirst: 'bool' = False, errors: 'object | None' = None) -> 'str | None'

Parse a datetime and convert it to ISO datetime format: yyyy-mm-ddTHH:MM:SS
- dayfirst=True: treat xx as the day in xx/yy/zz
- yearfirst=True: treat xx as the year in xx/yy/zz
- errors=r.IGNORE to ignore values that cannot be parsed
- errors=r.SET_NULL to set values that cannot be parsed to null

You can use these recipes like so:

sqlite-utils convert my.db mytable mycolumn \
    'r.jsonsplit(value, delimiter=":")'

Arguments:
- `DB_PATH` (file; required)
- `TABLE` (text; required)
- `COLUMNS...` (text; required)
- `CODE` (text; required)

Options:
- `--import TEXT` (repeatable): Python modules to import
- `--dry-run`: Show results of running this against first 10 rows
- `--multi`: Populate columns for keys in returned dictionary
- `--where TEXT`: Optional where clause
- `-p, --param TEXT TEXT` (repeatable): Named :parameters for where clause
- `--output TEXT`: Optional separate column to populate with the output
- `--output-type [integer|float|blob|text]` (default: text): Column type to use for the output column
- `--drop`: Drop original column afterwards
- `-s, --silent`: Don't show a progress bar
- `--pdb`: Open pdb debugger on first error

## `sqlite-utils create-table [OPTIONS] PATH TABLE COLUMNS...`

Add a table with the specified columns. Columns should be specified using
name, type pairs, for example:

    sqlite-utils create-table my.db people \
        id integer \
        name text \
        height real \
        photo blob --pk id

Valid column types are text, integer, real, float, blob and any.

Arguments:

Options:

- `--ignore`: If table already exists, do nothing
- `--replace`: If table already exists, replace it
- `--transform`: If table already exists, try to transform the schema
- `--strict`: Apply STRICT mode to created table

## `sqlite-utils insert [OPTIONS] PATH TABLE [FILE]`

Insert records from FILE into a table, creating the table if it
does not already exist.

Example:

    echo '{"name": "Lila"}' | sqlite-utils insert data.db chickens -

By default the input is expected to be a JSON object or array of objects.

- Use --nl for newline-delimited JSON objects
- Use --csv or --tsv for comma-separated or tab-separated input
- Use --lines to write each incoming line to a column called "line"
- Use --text to write the entire input to a column called "text"

Use --type column-name type to override the type automatically chosen
when the table is created.

You can also use --convert to pass a fragment of Python code that will
be used to convert each input.

Your Python code will be passed a "row" variable representing the
imported row, and can return a modified row.

This example uses just the name, latitude and longitude columns from
a CSV file, converting name to upper case and latitude and longitude
to floating point numbers:

    sqlite-utils insert plants.db plants plants.csv --csv --convert '
      return {
        "name": row["name"].upper(),
        "latitude": float(row["latitude"]),
        "longitude": float(row["longitude"]),
      }'

If you are using --lines your code will be passed a "line" variable,
and for --text a "text" variable.

When using --text your function can return an iterator of rows to
insert. This example inserts one record per word in the input:

    echo 'A bunch of words' | sqlite-utils insert words.db words - \
      --text --convert '({"word": w} for w in text.split())'

Instead of a FILE you can use --code to provide a block of Python code
that defines the rows to insert, as either a rows() function that yields
dictionaries or a "rows" iterable. --code can also be a path to a .py file:

    sqlite-utils insert data.db creatures --code '
    def rows():
        yield {"id": 1, "name": "Cleo"}
        yield {"id": 2, "name": "Suna"}
    ' --pk id

Arguments:
- `PATH` (file; required)
- `TABLE` (text; required)
- `[FILE]` (file)

Options:
- `--pk TEXT` (repeatable): Columns to use as the primary key, e.g. id
- `--code TEXT`: Python code defining a rows() function or iterable of rows to insert
- `--nl`: Expect newline-delimited JSON
- `-c, --csv`: Expect CSV input
- `--tsv`: Expect TSV input
- `--empty-null`: Treat empty strings as NULL
- `--text`: Treat input as a single value called 'text'
- `--convert TEXT`: Python code to convert each item
- `--import TEXT` (repeatable): Python modules to import
- `--delimiter TEXT`: Delimiter to use for CSV files
- `--quotechar TEXT`: Quote character to use for CSV/TSV
- `--sniff`: Detect delimiter and quote character
- `--no-headers`: CSV file has no header row
- `--batch-size INT` (default: 100): Commit every X records
- `--stop-after INT`: Stop after X records
- `--alter`: Alter existing table to add any missing columns
- `--type TEXT [INTEGER|TEXT|FLOAT|REAL|BLOB|ANY]` (repeatable): Column types to use when creating the table
- `--no-detect-types`: Treat all CSV/TSV columns as TEXT
- `--analyze`: Run ANALYZE at the end of this operation
- `--silent`: Do not show progress bar
- `--strict`: Apply STRICT mode to created table
- `--ignore`: Ignore records if pk already exists
- `--replace`: Replace records if pk already exists
- `--truncate`: Truncate table before inserting records, if table already exists
- Shared options: `--flatten`, `--lines`, `--encoding`, `--not-null`, `--default`, `--load-extension`

## `sqlite-utils insert-files [OPTIONS] PATH TABLE FILE_OR_DIR...`

Insert one or more files using BLOB columns in the specified table

    sqlite-utils insert-files pics.db images *.gif \
        -c name:name \
        -c content:content \
        -c content_hash:sha256 \
        -c created:ctime_iso \
        -c modified:mtime_iso \
        -c size:size \
        --pk name

- `PATH` (file; required)
- `TABLE` (text; required)
- `FILE_OR_DIR...` (path; required)

Options:
- `-c, --column TEXT` (repeatable): Column definitions for the table
- `--pk TEXT` (repeatable): Column to use as primary key
- `--alter`: Alter table to add missing columns
- `--replace`: Replace files with matching primary key
- `--upsert`: Upsert files with matching primary key
- `--name TEXT`: File name to use
- `--text`: Store file content as TEXT, not BLOB
- `-s, --silent`: Don't show a progress bar
- Shared options: `--encoding`, `--load-extension`

## `sqlite-utils memory [OPTIONS] [PATHS...] SQL`

Execute SQL query against an in-memory database, optionally populated by imported data

To import data from CSV, TSV or JSON files pass them on the command-line:

    sqlite-utils memory one.csv two.json \
        "select * from one join two on one.two_id = two.id"

For data piped into the tool from standard input, use "-" or "stdin":

    cat animals.csv | sqlite-utils memory - \
        "select * from stdin where species = 'dog'"

The format of the data will be automatically detected. You can specify the format
explicitly using :json, :csv, :tsv or :nl (for newline-delimited JSON) - for example:

    cat animals.csv | sqlite-utils memory stdin:csv places.dat:nl \
        "select * from stdin where place_id in (select id from places)"

Use --schema to view the SQL schema of any imported files:

    sqlite-utils memory animals.csv --schema

Arguments:
- `[PATHS...]` (file)
- `SQL` (text; required)

Options:
- `--attach TEXT FILE` (repeatable): Additional databases to attach - specify alias and filepath
- `--flatten`: Flatten nested JSON objects, so {"foo": {"bar": 1}} becomes {"foo_bar": 1}
- `--nl`: Output newline-delimited JSON
- `--arrays`: Output rows as arrays instead of objects
- `--csv`: Output CSV
- `--tsv`: Output TSV
- `-t, --table`: Output as a formatted table
- `-r, --raw`: Raw output, first column of first row
- `--raw-lines`: Raw output, first column of each row
- `-p, --param TEXT TEXT` (repeatable): Named :parameters for SQL query
- `--encoding TEXT`: Character encoding for CSV input, defaults to utf-8
- `-n, --no-detect-types`: Treat all CSV/TSV columns as TEXT
- `--schema`: Show SQL schema for in-memory database
- `--dump`: Dump SQL for in-memory database
- `--save FILE`: Save in-memory database to this file
- `--analyze`: Analyze resulting tables and output results
- Shared options: `--functions`, `--no-headers`, `--fmt`, `--json-cols`, `--ascii`, `--load-extension`

## `sqlite-utils migrate [OPTIONS] DB_PATH [MIGRATIONS...]`

Apply pending database migrations.

Usage:

    sqlite-utils migrate database.db

This will find the migrations.py file in the current directory
or subdirectories and apply any pending migrations.

Or pass paths to one or more migrations.py files directly:

    sqlite-utils migrate database.db path/to/migrations.py

Pass --list to see a list of applied and pending migrations
without applying them.

Use --stop-before migration_set:name to stop before a
migration. This option can be used multiple times.

Arguments:
- `DB_PATH` (file; required)
- `[MIGRATIONS...]` (path)

Options:
- `--stop-before TEXT` (repeatable): Stop before applying this migration. Use set:name to target a migration set.
- `--list`: List migrations without running them
- `-v, --verbose`: Show verbose output

## `sqlite-utils optimize [OPTIONS] PATH [TABLES...]`

Optimize all full-text search tables and then run VACUUM - should shrink the database file

Example:

    sqlite-utils optimize chickens.db

Arguments:
- `PATH` (file; required)
- `[TABLES...]` (text)

Options:
- `--no-vacuum`: Don't run VACUUM
- Shared options: `--load-extension`

## `sqlite-utils query [OPTIONS] PATH SQL`

Execute SQL query and return the results as JSON

Example:

    sqlite-utils data.db \
        "select * from chickens where age > :age" \
        -p age 1

Pass "-" as the SQL to read the query from standard input:

    echo "select * from chickens" | sqlite-utils data.db -

Arguments:
- `PATH` (file; required)
- `SQL` (text; required)

Options:
- `--attach TEXT FILE` (repeatable): Additional databases to attach - specify alias and filepath
- `--nl`: Output newline-delimited JSON
- `--arrays`: Output rows as arrays instead of objects
- `--csv`: Output CSV
- `--tsv`: Output TSV
- `-t, --table`: Output as a formatted table
- `-r, --raw`: Raw output, first column of first row
- `--raw-lines`: Raw output, first column of each row
- `-p, --param TEXT TEXT` (repeatable): Named :parameters for SQL query
- Shared options: `--no-headers`, `--fmt`, `--json-cols`, `--ascii`, `--functions`, `--load-extension`

## `sqlite-utils transform [OPTIONS] PATH TABLE`

Transform a table beyond the capabilities of ALTER TABLE

Example:

    sqlite-utils transform mydb.db mytable \
        --drop column1 \
        --rename column2 column_renamed

Arguments:
- `PATH` (file; required)
- `TABLE` (text; required)

Options:
- `--type TEXT [INTEGER|TEXT|FLOAT|REAL|BLOB|ANY]` (repeatable): Change column type to INTEGER, TEXT, FLOAT, REAL, BLOB or ANY
- `--drop TEXT` (repeatable): Drop this column
- `--rename TEXT TEXT` (repeatable): Rename this column to X
- `-o, --column-order TEXT` (repeatable): Reorder columns
- `--not-null TEXT` (repeatable): Set this column to NOT NULL
- `--not-null-false TEXT` (repeatable): Remove NOT NULL from this column
- `--pk TEXT` (repeatable): Make this column the primary key
- `--pk-none`: Remove primary key (convert to rowid table)
- `--default TEXT TEXT` (repeatable): Set default value for this column
- `--default-none TEXT` (repeatable): Remove default from this column
- `--add-foreign-key TEXT TEXT TEXT` (repeatable): Add a foreign key constraint from a column to another table with another column
- `--drop-foreign-key TEXT` (repeatable): Drop foreign key constraint for this column
- `--strict / --no-strict`: Enable or disable STRICT mode (default: preserve current mode)
- `--sql`: Output SQL without executing it
- Shared options: `--load-extension`

## `sqlite-utils upsert [OPTIONS] PATH TABLE [FILE]`

Upsert records based on their primary key. Works like 'insert' but if
an incoming record has a primary key that matches an existing record
the existing record will be updated.

If the table already exists and has a primary key, --pk can be omitted.

Use --type column-name type to override the type automatically chosen
when the table is created.

Example:

    echo '[
        {"id": 1, "name": "Lila"},
        {"id": 2, "name": "Suna"}
    ]' | sqlite-utils upsert data.db chickens - --pk id

Arguments:
- `PATH` (file; required)
- `TABLE` (text; required)
- `[FILE]` (file)

Options:
- `--pk TEXT` (repeatable): Columns to use as the primary key, e.g. id
- `--code TEXT`: Python code defining a rows() function or iterable of rows to insert
- `--nl`: Expect newline-delimited JSON
- `-c, --csv`: Expect CSV input
- `--tsv`: Expect TSV input
- `--empty-null`: Treat empty strings as NULL
- `--text`: Treat input as a single value called 'text'
- `--convert TEXT`: Python code to convert each item
- `--import TEXT` (repeatable): Python modules to import
- `--delimiter TEXT`: Delimiter to use for CSV files
- `--quotechar TEXT`: Quote character to use for CSV/TSV
- `--sniff`: Detect delimiter and quote character
- `--no-headers`: CSV file has no header row
- `--batch-size INT` (default: 100): Commit every X records
- `--stop-after INT`: Stop after X records
- `--alter`: Alter existing table to add any missing columns
- `--type TEXT [INTEGER|TEXT|FLOAT|REAL|BLOB|ANY]` (repeatable): Column types to use when creating the table
- `--no-detect-types`: Treat all CSV/TSV columns as TEXT
- `--analyze`: Run ANALYZE at the end of this operation
- `--silent`: Do not show progress bar
- `--strict`: Apply STRICT mode to created table
- Shared options: `--flatten`, `--lines`, `--encoding`, `--not-null`, `--default`, `--load-extension`
